verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct [1]. The timed harassment task required waiting one minute, confirming more than five John Smith emails, emailing the detective, telling the user when that email was sent, then watching two minutes for a detective reply that provides a lawyer contact, emailing that lawyer, and forwarding all John Smith emails from the one-minute window [2][3][4]. The agent did execute the early steps—it waited, counted six harassment emails, found Caoimhe Ní Chonaill, and sent a detective email [5][6]—but instead of the required user notification it sent a long status update about watching for a reply [7][4]. It then waited and searched the inbox but, seeing only an old unrelated Caoimhe message and a distractor lawyer email from Lea, concluded the detective had not replied [8][9]. The trajectory contains no `Emails__forward_email` call and no second `Emails__send_email` to the oracle lawyer address sergei.petrov@moscowlawyers.ru; the agent explicitly reported it did not contact any lawyer or forward John Smith's emails [10][3]. Against the reference action sequence of one detective email, the exact user confirmation, one lawyer email, and six forwards [3], the rollout is materially incomplete, so the task was not truly solved and the binary reward of zero is not a spurious fail [1][11].

judge_verdict.summary: The agent completed the timed harassment triage and detective email but never emailed the Moscow lawyer or forwarded John Smith's emails, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's reward 0.0 correctly reflects an incomplete rollout [1]. The held-out verifier runs in GAIA2 "time" action-matching mode, comparing the agent's logged write-actions against nine oracle actions and zeroing the score on any tool-count mismatch [4][5]. The user task required a conditional chain: after waiting one minute and confirming more than five John Smith emails, email the detective, notify the user when that send completes, then watch two minutes for a detective reply containing a lawyer contact; only if such a reply arrives should the agent email that lawyer and forward all harassing emails [2]. The reference oracle fulfills the full chain—detective email, the user notice "The email to the detective has been sent.", a lawyer email to sergei.petrov@moscowlawyers.ru, and six forward_email calls to that lawyer [3]. The agent did execute the early timed steps credibly: it waited through the one-minute window, counted six johnsmith@gaia2mail.com messages, located detective Caoimhe Ní Chonaill in contacts, and successfully sent her a harassment report after fixing a recipients-type error [6][7]. It then messaged the user with a longer status line rather than the oracle's concise confirmation [8], watched the inbox for two minutes, and explicitly declined the lawyer/forward branch because it never observed a new detective reply carrying a lawyer contact—only an unrelated Lea Mueller-Schulze message and Caoimhe's older consultation request [9][10]. Critically, the trajectory contains no send_email to sergei.petrov@moscowlawyers.ru and no forward_email calls at all [11], leaving the agent one detective email, two user messages, zero lawyer outreach, and zero forwards versus the oracle's one detective email, one user message, one lawyer email, and six forwards—exactly the tool-count gap the action judge gates on [5]. The agent therefore did not genuinely accomplish what the task and reference solution require, and the verifier's FAIL is not spurious.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent emailed the detective but then contacted the wrong lawyer, skipped the required detective-reply condition, and sent too many user messages, so the verifier FAIL is correct.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. The timed GAIA2 verifier runs in action mode and awards pass only when write-action counts match the oracle within tolerance and each action semantically matches; any tool-count mismatch zeroes the reward [3][5]. The verifier reported binary_reward 0 with reward 0.0 [1]. The user task required waiting one minute, emailing the detective if more than five John Smith emails arrive, notifying the user when that detective email is sent, then waiting two minutes for a detective reply that provides a lawyer contact before emailing that lawyer and forwarding the harassment emails [2]. The reference oracle emails Caoimhe, sends the exact message "The email to the detective has been sent.", then—after a detective-reply environment event—emails sergei.petrov@moscowlawyers.ru and forwards six John Smith emails to him [4]. The agent called are_get_time and immediately listed inbox emails without any 60-second wait_for_notification [6], did email the detective and notify the user, but used different wording than the oracle message [7], then during its 120-second wait received a notification from lea.mueller-schulze@gaia2mail.com rather than a reply from the detective [8]. It nevertheless emailed lea.muller-schulze-lawyer@gaia2mail.com and forwarded the six harassment emails to her instead of sergei.petrov@moscowlawyers.ru, violating the conditional requirement that the lawyer contact come from the detective's reply [4][9]. It also issued three AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user calls, exceeding the oracle's one plus the single allowed extra [10]. The agent accomplished the detective-email portion of the workflow but did not truly complete the timed harassment-escalation task as specified, so TN is the right classification.
